question: In the minimum CET1 capital ratio requirement that Belfius Bank had to meet for 2025 (consolidated, before Pillar 2 Guidance), what Pillar 2 add-on is counted, how does it relate to the total Pillar 2 Requirement (P2R) set by the supervisor for 2025, and how is the difference explained?
reference_answer: The 2025 minimum CET1 capital ratio requirement of 10.88% (before Pillar 2 Guidance) includes a Pillar II requirement of 1.15% (1.22% in 2024), i.e. only the CET1-eligible part of the P2R. The total P2R for 2025 was 2.02% (reviewed down from an initial 2.24% set in December 2024; 2.16% in 2024). The difference arises because the 'general' P2R of 2% is only required to be held in the form of 56.25% CET1 capital, plus a prudential add-on for non-performing exposures of 2 bps which must be held fully in CET1 (2% x 56.25% = 1.125% plus 0.02% = about 1.15%). Pillar 2 Guidance of 1.00% is not part of the 10.88% (with it the figure is 11.88%).

evidence.text: Pillar II requirement............................................................... 1.22% 1.15%… MINIMUM CET 1 CAPITAL RATIO REQUIREMENT ..................... 10.93% 10.88%… a Pillar 2 Requirement (P2R) of 1.15% (after split of 2.02% P2R);

The Pillar 2 Requirement (P2R) was initially set in December 2024 at 2.24% and subsequently reviewed to… 2.02% (to compare with 2.16% in 2024) to be held in the form of 56.25% CET 1 capital for the “general” P2R… of 2% and including a prudential add-on for non-performing exposures of 2 bps to be held in the form of CET… 1 capital.

question: At the end of 2025, on a consolidated basis for Belfius Bank and expressed as a percentage of total risk exposure amount (TREA, binding targets including the combined buffer requirement), which MREL cushion was larger: the realised total MREL over its binding target, or the realised MREL subordination over its binding target? Give both cushions and the difference in percentage points.
reference_answer: The subordination cushion was larger. Total MREL: realised 31.2% of TREA (EUR 22.5 billion) versus a binding target of 28.91% (including the CBR), a cushion of 2.29 percentage points. MREL subordination: realised 22.7% of TREA (EUR 16.3 billion) versus a binding target of 18.73% (including the CBR), a cushion of 3.97 percentage points. The subordination cushion exceeds the total MREL cushion by 1.68 percentage points (3.97 - 2.29).

evidence.text: Expressed in TREA terms, Belfius realised MREL… of EUR 22.5 billion amounted to 31.2%, compared with the binding target of 28.91% (including the CBR).… In the same way, Belfius MREL subordination of EUR 16.3 billion amounted to 22.7% of TREA, compared… with a binding target of 18.73% (including the CBR).

question: Was Belfius Bank's consolidated effective tax rate for 2025 under IFRS (total tax expense divided by net income before tax) above the statutory tax rate that the prospectus cites? Give the ratio to one decimal place.
reference_answer: Yes. Total tax expense of EUR 436,308,981 divided by net income before tax of EUR 1,598,462,817 gives an effective tax rate of 27.3% for 2025, above the 25% statutory tax rate cited by Belfius (the prospectus describes the effective rate as slightly above the statutory rate, due to a higher result before tax and untaxed capital gains in 2024).

evidence.text: showing an effective tax rate slightly above the statutory tax rate (25%).

question: Under the Terms and Conditions of Belfius Bank's EUR 25 billion EMTN Programme, if the Final Terms of a Note specify 'Amortised Face Amount' and the Note becomes immediately repayable after an Event of Default, how is the amount payable determined, and which event gives a Noteholder the right to demand that immediate repayment?
reference_answer: The 'Event of Default Redemption Amount' is, where 'Amortised Face Amount' is specified, 'an amount calculated in accordance with Condition 3(b)'. Under Condition 3(b), the Amortised Face Amount is the scheduled Zero Coupon Note Redemption Amount of the Note on the Maturity Date discounted at a rate per annum equal to the Amortisation Yield compounded annually (for periods of less than one year, the Day Count Fraction in the Final Terms applies), plus accrued interest if applicable. A holder may give written notice that its Notes are immediately repayable upon a dissolution or liquidation of the Issuer under Belgian law (bankruptcy, judicial liquidation or voluntary liquidation, other than one connected with a reconstruction, merger or amalgamation where the continuing corporation assumes all liabilities). A payment default continuing 30 days or more only allows a holder to institute proceedings for dissolution or liquidation of the Issuer in Belgium, and a resolution action by the Relevant Resolution Authority does not entitle holders to accelerate.

evidence.text: If default is made in the payment of any principal or interest due in respect of the Subordinated Notes or the… Senior Notes and such default continues for a period of 30 days or more after the due date, any holder of the… In the event of a dissolution or liquidation of the Issuer including, without limiting the generality of the… give written notice to the Paying Agent at its specified office that its relevant Note(s) is (are) immediately

repayable, whereupon the Event of Default Redemption Amount of such Note(s) together (if applicable) with… accrued interest to the date of payment shall become immediately due and payable.… shall not entitle the holders of the relevant Notes to accelerate the Issuer’s payment obligations thereunder.… “Amortised Face Amount” is specified in the applicable Final Terms, an amount calculated in accordance with… Condition 3(b) above.

(ii)    Subject to sub-paragraph (iii) below, the “Amortised Face Amount” of any such Note shall be… the scheduled Zero Coupon Note Redemption Amount of such Note on the Maturity Date discounted at a rate per annum (expressed as a percentage) equal to the Amortisation Yield… compounded annually.… Where such calculation is to be made for a period of less than one year, it shall be made on the… basis of the Day Count Fraction set out in the applicable Final Terms.

question: According to the risk factors in Belfius Bank's EMTN Base Prospectus, how many cumulative conditions must be met before the Relevant Resolution Authority can exercise its bail-in powers over the Notes, what are they, and how many alternative circumstances can support the determination that Belfius Bank is 'failing or likely to fail'?
reference_answer: Three cumulative conditions: (a) the relevant regulator or Relevant Resolution Authority has determined that Belfius Bank is failing or is likely to fail; (b) having regard to timing and other circumstances, there is no reasonable prospect that any alternative private sector measures or supervisory action would prevent the failure within a reasonable timeframe; and (c) a resolution action is necessary in the public interest. Condition (a) is met if one or more of four circumstances is present: (i) Belfius infringes, or will in the near future infringe, the requirements for continuing authorisation in a way that would justify withdrawal of authorisation (including losses depleting all or a significant amount of own funds); (ii) its assets are, or will in the near future be, less than its liabilities; (iii) it is, or will in the near future be, unable to pay its debts or other liabilities as they fall due; (iv) it requests extraordinary public financial support.

question: Belfius Bank's EMTN Base Prospectus says its consolidated CET1 ratio rose between end-2024 and end-2025. Does Belfius's 2025 Pillar 3 report show the same direction of change, and if not, what reference point and regulatory basis explain the difference?
reference_answer: Not on the Pillar 3 reference point. Both documents give a CET1 ratio of 15.87% at 31 December 2025. The prospectus compares it with the published end-2024 ratio of 15.38% under CRR 2/CRD 5 and reports an increase of +49 bps (lower total risk exposure amount, EUR -3.0 billion to EUR 72.1 billion, partly offset by CET1 capital EUR -111 million). The Pillar 3 report compares it with the pro forma end-2024 ratio under CRR 3/CRD 6 (Basel IV) and reports a decrease of 29 bps (lower prudential capital -15 bps, higher risk exposures -14 bps). The gap is the Basel IV transition, which added 78 bps to the end-2024 ratio (the published 15.38%, slightly adjusted from 15.39% after a late Corep correction, plus 78 bps gives a pro forma ratio of about 16.16%; +49 bps versus -29 bps differ by 78 bps).
